headline: session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions, always by printing decision:block JSON and exiting 0: the agent-armed 🔧 continuation (emitted at 1336, or 1334 with mail; ends via kill phrase, `clear` or CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX), the mechanical 🔧 arm for this session's own uncommitted files (armed 1072, CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or CC_MECH_MAX), the 📦 ship floor (1187/1199, CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX), the 🚀 ship floor (1189/1199, same switches) and the wake floor (895, CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX or CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S); every one of them also stands down on an operator kill phrase.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions, all by printing {decision:"block"} (it never blocks through its exit code): (1) a sentinel the agent set with `set` exists (L1334/1336), (2) the mechanical arm arms on this session's uncommitted writes and falls through to that same block, (3) the 📦 ship floor for this session's committed-but-unlanded commits (L1187/1199), (4) the 🚀 ship floor for work that landed but is not live (L1189/1199), and (5) the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (L895). The off switches are CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 and CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0; the sentinel path has none, but a kill phrase or CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX=0 lets its stops through.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 4 conditions, always as decision:block JSON with exit 0 (exit 2 appears only on the CLI path). (1) An agent-armed sentinel blocks at lines 1334/1336; it is disabled by the kill-switch phrase, `clear`, a sid mismatch, or the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap. (2) The mechanical arm (own uncommitted writes on the 🔧 rung) re-uses that block at 1334/1336; it is disabled by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0 or the CC_MECH_MAX budget. (3) The ship floor (📦/🚀 own work) blocks at 1199; it is disabled by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0 or the CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX budget. (4) The wake floor (no inbox watcher armed) blocks at 894-895; it is disabled by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, the CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX budget or the CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S backoff. The kill-switch phrase also stops conditions 2-4, and the assignee and teardown-marker abstains stop conditions 2-4 as well.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop under 5 conditions. Ship floor 📦 is committed-but-unlanded work this session wrote (:1187/1199; CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0, CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX). Ship floor 🚀 is landed work that is not live (:1189/1199). The wake floor fires when the session goes idle with no inbox watcher armed on first idle, with pending mail or with open custody (:894; CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S). The mechanical 🔧 arm fires on uncommitted files this session wrote (:1072→1334; CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, CC_MECH_MAX). The agent-armed sentinel continuation fires after `session-continue.sh set` (:1304/1334; clear, the kill phrase, sid mismatch, CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX). All blocks exit 0 with decision:block JSON; exit 2 occurs only in the CLI modes.

The session-continue.sh Stop hook blocks a stop under 5 conditions: (1) an agent-armed continuation sentinel, blocked at 1334/1336 and capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX; (2) the mechanical arm for uncommitted files this session wrote, armed at 1072 and blocked through the same path (CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, CC_MECH_MAX); (3) the ship floor on 📦, committed but unlanded work it wrote, at 1199; (4) the ship floor on 🚀, landed but not live, at 1199 (both ship floors: CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0, CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX); and (5) the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed, at 895 (CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S). The kill-switch phrase in the last user message disarms all five.

In Stop mode, session-continue.sh blocks under five conditions and always exits 0, sending the block as {decision:"block"} JSON: (1) a sentinel armed with `set` (:1336/:1334; turned off by the kill phrase, a SID mismatch or CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX=0), (2) a sentinel armed by mechanical_arm for this session's uncommitted files, which blocks through the same path (CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, CC_MECH_MAX budget), (3) the 📦 ship floor and (4) the 🚀 ship floor (:1199; CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0, CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX, latched once per HEAD commit), and (5) the wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (:895; CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX, CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S). The operator kill phrase (KILL_RE :348) turns off all five, and every exit 2 in the file is on a CLI path, never on a Stop.

session-continue.sh blocks a stop in 5 cases, all through a decision:block JSON with exit 0. (1) A continuation the agent armed with `set`, emitted at :1334/:1336, bounded by the CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX cap (8 by default). (2) The mechanical arm for uncommitted files this session wrote, which arms at :1072 and blocks through the same lines, turned off by CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0. (3) and (4) The ship floor for 📦 unlanded or 🚀 not-live work, at :1199, turned off by CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0. (5) The wake floor for going idle with no inbox watcher, at :895, turned off by CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0. An operator kill-switch phrase (KILL_RE at :348) overrides all five, and the exit-2 paths at :116, :130 and :216 only run in CLI mode, so they never block a stop.

The Stop hook blocks under 5 conditions. (1) Agent-armed 🔧 continuation (:1334/:1336, capped by CLAUDE_CONTINUE_MAX, removed by `clear`). (2) Mechanical 🔧 arm on this session's uncommitted files (arms at :1072, blocks via the continuation site; off with CC_MECH_CONTINUE=0, budget CC_MECH_MAX). (3) Ship floor on 📦 and (4) ship floor on 🚀 (:1199; off with CC_SHIP_FLOOR=0, budget CC_SHIP_FLOOR_MAX, fires once per HEAD sha). (5) Wake floor when no inbox watcher is armed (:895; off with CC_WAKE_FLOOR=0, limited by CC_WAKE_FLOOR_MAX and CC_WAKE_FLOOR_TTL_S). All five are also suppressed by an operator kill-switch phrase.

I found 7 real bugs in rotate-logs.sh by reading it; I did not run it. The worst is that `cd $dir` is unquoted and unchecked, so a missing or wrong argument makes the script delete .gz files in $HOME or the caller's directory. Next come `xargs rm` splitting names with spaces and deleting the wrong files, and an off-by-one in `tail -n +$keep` that keeps only keep-1 archives (none when keep=1). The rest: gzip refuses to overwrite an existing app.log.gz so a log stops rotating, `-mtime +1` only matches files at least 48h old, `$(ls)` and the unquoted test break names with spaces, and retention counts every *.gz in the directory.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs. The worst: an unchecked `cd $dir` (line 5) lets line 11 delete .gz files in $HOME or the current directory; `tail -n +$keep` keeps one archive too few, and with keep=1 deletes them all; `*.gz` and `xargs` delete unrelated or wrongly split files; `-mtime +1` means 2 or more days old; the `ls`/unquoted `[ ]` loop breaks on filenames with spaces; and `gzip` collides on a second rotation of the same log name.

rotate-logs.sh has 7 real bugs. The worst is the unchecked `cd $dir` on line 5: if it fails or $1 is missing, the script runs in the wrong directory and deletes .gz files there. Next are three bugs that keep archives wrong or delete the wrong ones: an off-by-one in `tail -n +$keep` that keeps only keep-1, a `*.gz` glob that also prunes non-log archives, and a fixed archive name that makes gzip refuse the next rotation. The rest are lower severity: `-mtime +1` really means 2 or more days old, filenames with spaces or a leading dash get word-split (and xargs can rm the wrong file), and the script always prints success and exits 0.
